findings.how: Round 1: added an optional WindowSystem.systemDialogReason(). macOS gives 'secure keyboard entry is on in <app> …' when secure input is on and no security prompt is up. The worker's refusal and audit reason use it, and so does Perception's no-screenshot note. systemDialogOpen() still decides and still fails closed. inspectMac gained a Secure input row, and the doctor row uses the same words. Round 2 (bc1b7a5): when another app (Safari) holds secure input, the setup-check row no longer reads as if Safari had a Terminal menu. It now uses the doctor's wording, '(Terminal: Terminal menu › Secure Keyboard Entry)'.

Round 2: the environment-platforms expectation (Terminal and Safari holders) was updated. It failed on the old wording and passes now.

findings.how: Decided on purpose to keep setContentProtection on Windows and macOS, so there is no code change. The protection keeps unredacted command output and password cards out of any other app's recordings. Turning it off in a 'remote session' would not help: TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Quick Assist and VNC capture the console session, and Electron's docs say Remote Desktop already shows these windows. The cost is now documented as limitation L27 in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md (which tools show a blank space, and where to approve and type instead), and L11 points to it. The verifier raised nothing about it in round 2.
findings.test: None. This is a documented decision, and windows.ts imports Electron, so it can't be unit-tested. The decision was checked against setContentProtection in node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts.

findings.how: Round 1: the macOS catalogue reads each bundle's localized names for the first preferred system language it has, from InfoPlist.loctable (macOS 14 and later) or <lang>.lproj/InfoPlist.strings, using a new parseStringsFile() for the binary, XML and text forms in UTF-8 and UTF-16. It adds those names to keywords (what open_app searches) and to programs (what the worker matches a new window against). Round 2 (fad2daf): test/integration/darwin-system.test.ts now runs darwinApps({ languages: () => ['de-DE'] }).list() on the real catalogue. It expects com.apple.calculator's programs and keywords to contain 'rechner', com.apple.systempreferences's to contain 'systemeinstellungen', and find('Rechner') to be com.apple.calculator. On a miss it prints that bundle's German resources, so CI shows the real layout.
findings.test: Round 1: the darwin-system-apps and darwin-system-plist unit tests failed before the fix and pass now. Round 2: the darwin-system case is skipped on this Linux machine. It runs on macOS CI (macos-15 with EMBER_MACSYS_TEST=1), so whether real Apple bundles match is only proven there.

findings.how: Round 1: added isWaylandSession(). In a Wayland session the system-dialog check is on with WAYLAND_REASON: no screenshots and no borrowed mouse or keyboard, while reading apps carries on. sessionGreeting() replaces 'I'll stay by your cursor', and settings opens on a login start while the session check fails. Round 2 (7528b96): openLinuxWindows is back as it was, and only the Linux platform's openWindows (app/main/platform/linux/index.ts) adds the Wayland check. The SSH remote's desktop child (desktop-child.ts) is therefore unaffected. Round 2 (892ee39): each case now has its own first-person line. Service session: 'I can't work in this session: start me from your desktop, not as a service.' No or unreachable X display: 'I can't reach your desktop's display: start me from inside your desktop session.' The Wayland line is unchanged.
findings.test: Round 1: the environment.test and Linux window-system tests failed before the fix and pass now, plus a scratch Xvfb run as a login start. Round 2: the Wayland tests moved to platform-linux.test (openWindows: check on for Wayland; Xorg, Xvfb, xrdp and ssh -X unchanged; null when X can't open). platform-linux-window-system now checks that openLinuxWindows adds no check of its own. findings.how: Round 1: when the keychain refuses (Deny or Cancel), TokenStore.load() sets unreadable and keeps the file. On macOS the signed-out status then says 'macOS didn't let Ember read its saved sign-in … choose Always Allow'. Round 2, verifier's second point (7a7ed42): TokenStore keeps the version of Ember that last opened or saved the sign-in in token-read-version, next to github-token.bin. The file is written only when the keyring lets Ember in. startBrain waits 800 ms and shows 'Reading your saved sign-in from the keychain…' only when firstReadSinceUpdate() says this version hasn't read it yet, so normal starts read at once with no message. Round 2, verifier's first point (bbb053d, 8b87989): load() is now async and resolveToken awaits it. With asyncDecrypt it opens the file with safeStorage.decryptStringAsync, still telling a refusal apart and keeping the file. main turns asyncDecrypt on for macOS only. Linux, Windows and the doctor read synchronously as before. The new darwin-system case (macOS CI only) seals a token with encryptString and opens it with decryptStringAsync, both directly and through TokenStore, and expects the same token with shouldReEncrypt false. The switch is in its own commit (8b87989) so the lead can revert it alone if that CI case fails. The README keychain note belongs to the docs package and is listed in forDocs.
findings.test: auth-save.test.ts: 'opens the saved sign-in with decryptStringAsync when asked to' failed on the previous auth.ts (expected 'gho_abc', got null) and passes now (17/17). The refusal and sync-fallback cases and the four firstReadSinceUpdate cases pass. The firstReadSinceUpdate cases failed before 7a7ed42. The darwin-system keychain case runs only on macOS CI.

verifierProblems.what: Partly fixed, as the fix agent says. The sign-out now says why, but the freeze is still there. TokenStore.load() calls the synchronous safeStorage.decryptString on the main process (auth.ts load(), reached from startBrain in main.ts around line 1573), so the overlay, the shortcuts and Stop stay frozen for as long as the macOS keychain prompt is open. The 800 ms pause only lets the windows come up first. The README keychain note (choose Always Allow next to the permission re-grant steps) is also still missing, and that file belongs to the docs package.
verifierProblems.fix: Lead: (1) Make sure the docs package's list gets the README update note: after every update macOS asks for the login keychain password for Ember Safe Storage; choose Always Allow. (2) Add a darwin-only test to test/integration/darwin-system.test.ts. It should seal a token with safeStorage.encryptString and open it with safeStorage.decryptStringAsync, and check result and shouldReEncrypt. If that passes on macOS CI, switch TokenStore.load to decryptStringAsync (an async load, awaited in resolveToken) so the prompt no longer blocks the main process.

verifierProblems.what: On every macOS start with a saved sign-in, not only after an update, startBrain waits KEYCHAIN_PAUSE_MS (800 ms) and shows 'Reading your saved sign-in from the keychain…' in the status line (main.ts, startBrain). The keychain only asks after the app's code identity changes (an update), so a normal start now flashes a keychain message and greets 0.8 s later for no reason.
verifierProblems.fix: Save app.getVersion() after a successful read (for example a small 'token-read-version' file next to github-token.bin, or a field in settings). Only pause and show the status when the saved version differs from the running one (the first start after an update) or is missing.

verifierProblems.what: The localized-name support is tested only on bundles the test builds itself (an XML loctable, UTF-16 text .strings). Nothing checks that real Apple bundles on macOS 13 and 14+ use these file names, these locale keys and these encodings: for example that /System/Applications/Calculator.app has de.lproj/InfoPlist.strings or an InfoPlist.loctable keyed 'de' that contains CFBundleDisplayName or CFBundleName. If the real layout differs, the fix silently adds no names.
verifierProblems.fix: In test/integration/darwin-system.test.ts (it already runs darwinApps() on macOS CI), add a case: darwinApps({ languages: () => ["de-DE"] }).list(). Expect com.apple.calculator's programs to contain "rechner" and com.apple.systempreferences's to contain "systemeinstellungen", and expect c.find(list, "Rechner")?.id to be com.apple.calculator.

verifierProblems.what: Copy: Windows 10 22H2's toggle is called “Allow desktop apps to access your microphone”, but the new setup-check row quotes the Windows 11 name, “Let desktop apps access your microphone”, next to the Windows 10 path. The doctor's fix line also puts the bracket in the middle of a menu path: “Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone (Settings › Privacy › Microphone on Windows 10) › Let desktop apps access your microphone”. Separately, the new voice-line button swallows a failed fix (home/main.ts: applyFix(fix).then(renderChecks, () => undefined)). The setup-check row's own button shows “Couldn't change it: …” in the same case.
verifierProblems.fix: Word the row as: “Turn on desktop apps' access to the microphone: Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone › Let desktop apps access your microphone (on Windows 10: Settings › Privacy › Microphone › Allow desktop apps to access your microphone).” Build the doctor fix the same way. Either keep a WINDOWS_MIC_PATH per Windows version, or have one constant that holds both whole paths. In the voice-fix click handler, on rejection show `Couldn't open it: ${ipcErrorText(err)}` through voiceLive or #voice-text, the same as the check row does.

verifierProblems.what: dpiMixed is true when the helper's thread and its process have different DPI awareness (win32/system/environment.ts: helper.dpi !== helper.processDpi). That does not change with monitor scale, so after the user sets every monitor to the same scale and restarts Ember, the Display scaling row and the doctor row still warn. The advice then looks as if it failed, and the user is pushed to report it even when clicks now land correctly.
verifierProblems.fix: Reword MIXED_SCALING_FIX so the note can stay without implying failure, for example: “Set every monitor to the same scale in Settings › System › Display, then restart Ember.
